rubric_notes: All a.22.1 families correct with sunids, consistent with bundle. Correctly states superfamily implies probable homology not detectable by sequence, that function cannot be transferred across families (TAFs/NF-Y are transcription factors), and that fold-only relatives do not exist in 2.08 because a.22 has one superfamily. Correctly separates H1/H5 (a.4.5.13), HU/IHF (a.55.1), H-NS (a.155.1), modifying enzymes, and notes structural evidence needed for new assignments. Omits Aq_328 from bacterial family listing (noncentral, bundle lacked that children page). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct family placements and superfamily a.204.1 (sunid 101386) with correct protein/species names and boundaries. Explains superfamily = probable common ancestry without family-level sequence evidence, that shared fold alone would not imply homology, and enumerates unsafe transfers (PR-ATP substrate, histidine pathway, MazG house-cleaning, catalytic residues, oligomeric state, template use). Hypothetical-protein and UNL ligand caveats correctly drawn from annotations. No material omissions.

Correct families, superfamily, fold, class, sunids, and duplication comment supported by bundle; correctly notes two c.55.1 domains per chain. Infers descent from one ancestral duplicated ATPase with shared nucleotide-binding mechanism and closure mode, and explicitly denies transfer of specific function, substrate specificity, cellular role, substrate-binding residues, regulatory sites, and oligomeric behaviour; fold c.55 membership implies topology only; template and external-evidence caveats included. Complete. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct hierarchy with sunids supported by bundle; superfamily interpreted as probable homology from the conserved bimetal site, families as divergence of chemistry; refuses cross-family transfer of function, metal, oligomeric state, or mechanism and names biochemical/spectroscopic and active-site evidence required. Notes a.25.1.2 internal heterogeneity and automated-match provenance. Minor speculative remark that a.25.1.4-9 were added on structural evidence is hedged and noncentral. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Families, sunids, Pfam, fold description and all curator comments match bundle. Hierarchy semantics explained; superfamily comment correctly read as describing canonical members; copper/ET transfer refused, reverse transfer also rejected; external evidence specified. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct families, sunids, superfamily and fold; empty superfamily comment record supported by bundle. Explains superfamily as curated common origin of the beta-grasp core and separate families as the signal of functional divergence; explicitly rejects annotating UBX/RBD as modifiers, RBD as p97 cofactor, Ras binding for ubiquitin/UBX, and cross-family binding-site/catalytic transfer; fold-level MoaD/ThiS caveat; automated-match provenance; requires sequence motifs and experimental data. Less evidence breadth than others but no missing material facts or errors.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct families, sunids, Pfam PF03709, fold description, KaiA annotation. Clearly separates superfamily-level probable homology from fold-level similarity, rejects phosphorelay signaling, decarboxylase catalysis, flavodoxin/FMN inference, and circadian function transfer, and identifies the wing as a structural/oligomerization element rather than the catalytic domain. Minor imprecision: refers to ODC catalytic core as 'TIM-barrel-like' though the classified c.23.1.4 entry is bacterial (Lactobacillus) ODC; hedged and not a SCOPe claim.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. All must-include items met: b.84.5 in fold b.84, five superfamilies with correct sunids, single family b.84.5.1 with two protein entries and correct example domains. Excellent asymmetric reading: separate superfamily withholds the homology claim, does not assert convergence; fold homology warning cited from bundle. Family vs superfamily semantics handled correctly; unsafe function/template transfers rejected. One noncentral imprecision: describes the bulge as 'wedged between' the b.49.1.2 barrel and the P-loop domain, whereas SCOPe boundaries place it as an insertion inside the discontinuous c.37.1.11 domain. The 'deterministic comparison ... same_fold' phrasing implies a compare endpoint not in the bundle, though the lowest shared node b.84 is derivable from the bundled parents of d3a5ca3 and d1bdoa_.

Correct hierarchy with sunids and Pfam xref supported by bundle; correctly interprets superfamily as the homology level and fold as architecture possibly convergent without asserting convergence; discusses all three curator comments including 'possible link' as hypothesis; names external evidence (profile-HMM/Pfam clan, conserved His positions, genomic context) and release-specificity. Families not enumerated but not required.

Identifiers, lineage, 12 named + c.2.1.0 family count, fold comment, family comments and PF02254 all match the bundle. Correctly reads superfamily as probable common ancestry inferred from structure plus binding mode rather than sequence, treats family as the stronger claim not shared here, and states fold alone is never evidence of ancestry. Explicitly lists non-transferable properties (EC number, catalytic residues, cofactor identity, oligomeric state, domain boundaries) and the external evidence to seek. Minor imprecision: describes c.2.1.0 members as assigned to existing families, when they are placed only at superfamily level without family assignment; noncentral. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Correct same-family facts and sunids, sound class k interpretation, no-transfer limits. Explicitly states the caveat arises only from class k and that SCOPe attaches no explicit warnings, missing the 'not a true family' curator comment on sunid 100905; decisive annotation ignored, bio <=2. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-14. Must_include met: 1.69 d1t1ja_ c.137.1.1 singleton fold verified vs 1f8y c.23.14.1; 2.08 d1t1ja1 c.23.14.2 vs c.23.14.1 shared superfamily verified with four-family listing; describes abolition of fold/superfamily nodes, re-parenting of the preserved family, and separately the tag-split boundary change, so the move is framed as a new superfamily-level homology hypothesis. Correct current SID with explicit note that d1t1ja_ and d1t1ja1 differ in range. Function and template caveats correct and fold-alone-is-not-homology stated. Noncentral imprecisions: labels the 1.69 superfamily with its later name N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like, speculative 'Nudix-adjacent' rationale not supported by any evidence, and says the change occurred 'in 1.75' though hedged as not queried (actually by 1.71).

All required content present and supported: l.1.1.1 artifact lineage for H:1-8, b.1.1.1 VH for H:9-111 with Fab NC10 comment, explicit statement that class-l similarity is not homology evidence and that only d1a14h1 supports homology inference, with fold-alone caveat. Statement that class l dates from 2.06 is plausible general knowledge. No material errors.

Concise but correct: 1.75 whole-chain d1acca_ in f.11.1.1 and the 2.08 pair with correct sunids, boundaries, and new fold sunids. Makes the module inference from PA14 family membership shared with a eukaryotic enzyme domain, keeps family and superfamily as the strong claims, rejects fold-only ancestry and function transfer, and requires release pinning and remapping. Does not identify 2.04 as the split release, and asserts a UniProt accession and a cluster representative for the chain without supporting retrieved evidence.

All five domains correct with boundaries and lineages; fold comment and singleton lineage supported by bundle; c.55.3.14 pre-existence with S. cerevisiae/human nodes shown. Interpretation covers mosaic evolution, reuse vs innovation, superfamily vs family strength, and explicit rejection of catalytic/acetyl-lysine function transfer; coverage and cryo-EM caveats stated. UniProt/length extras unverified but noncentral.

Biologically complete: shared family a.298.1.1 with full lineage, length as variable copy number of one roughly 34-residue unit, the canonical repeat record with d4cj9a_ as representative, the quoted 're' inconsistency definition, and the 'single repeat' comment. Good limits on specificity, template choice, identity statistics and fold-only inference. Factual deductions are noncentral: the claim that d4cj9a_ lacks a 're' flag because it is the canonical representative asserts a curatorial reason not present in the retrieved records, and the greater than 90 percent repeat identity figure and the 22-copy count are stated without support. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14.

Endpoint metadata correct and evidence-backed. Advises pinning release 2.08 and recording the specific stable or dated periodic label plus fetch date, explicitly rejecting bare 'current' as a moving pointer. Correctly distinguishes 2.08-stable (frozen curated freeze) from dated periodic updates that add automatically classified entries without changing stable nodes/identifiers. Mention of derived hit streams is minor and not a material error.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Correct lineage, ms flags, 1dn1 obsolete and automated match to d3c98b_, d1dn1a_ e.25.1.1 automated match, fold homology_implied_by_level=false, all bundle-supported. Reasoning complete: fold by curatorial extrapolation, spectrin warning as fold-level only, fourth helix conformational (H3 in closed state), representative selection d3c98b_, hit-count caveat, limits. Noncentral error: SNARE fusion complex given as 'h.1.5' (hedged); SCOPe uses h.1.15.1.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-14. Answers directly with correct level semantics: divergence within c.2.1 (noting CoA-binding and K+-channel members show superfamily membership does not license NAD-function transfer), separate folds as insufficient evidence with 'true independent origins or undetectable divergence is left open', ADP-ribosyltransferase/sirtuin example, strong explanation of why cofactor sites and short motifs are low-information, and integrated evidence requirements plus template/transfer limits. Sunids (c.2 51734, c.3 51904, c.4 51970, c.31 52466, d.166 56398, c.23.5 52218), comments and family lists match the bundle.

Correct on the required release contrast and on holding the claim at superfamily level with families b.18.1.36 and b.18.1.3 separate, and strong on limits: no function, calcium, catalytic or template transfer, release-pinned identifiers, and an explicit note that fold alone would be insufficient. It also usefully names the external evidence still needed. Deductions because several structural specifics are asserted beyond the retrieved records, including an unretrieved deterministic comparison result, a claimed ColG sunid-level b.18.1.36 family content, and detailed strand-order, buried-core and binding-site-position claims presented as evidence without retrieved or cited support; the curated PubMed note is cited but its Cry4Ba-not-Cry3A subtlety is not surfaced.

Uses bundle lineage, hf definition, structure-hits (empty, 1p7iA representative at 93% identity) and protein-node annotations correctly. Homology justified at protein/species level; hf explained as sequence-based retention despite non-exemplar fold; template, function-transfer, benchmark and representative-selection limits all covered with filtering on hf flags. Notes absence of FATCAT hits is not proof and that coordinates/literature are needed.

Lineage, fr flag, 50-residue ATOM sequence vs 104, both quality records match bundle. Correctly treats fr as a data-completeness warning not a homology warning, explains low coverage and depressed scores, SEQRES vs ATOM sequence use, fragment excluded/marked in profiles, AEROSPACI-driven choice would wrongly favour the fragment, choose a complete TF domain-2 from the same protein node, d1uc6a1 acceptable only with NMR quality caveat, fragment counted for census but not as complete structural observation, no function transfer. Noncentral factual error: misreads the 'complexed with cr9' comment as a 5G9/CR9 antibody fragment complex (cr9 is a ligand code; the H/L chains are protease/EGF domains), and builds an antibody-stabilization caveat on that premise. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct recommendation with clear level-by-level semantics (family confident ancestry, superfamily probable ancestry, fold topology only with possible convergence, class composition). States new fold is wrong unless core topology differs and that nesting a new family under an existing superfamily asserts unsupported ancestry. Treats placement as revisable hypothesis, lists merging evidence, warns that FATCAT hits are candidate evidence not proof, rejects fold-mate function transfer. Release facts stated (2.08, freeze 2021-07-28, 2.08-2026-08-16) are correct and not attributed to an unverified API call. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1; 2026-10-14.

Correct families/superfamily/fold with supported sunids and representatives (d1atpe_, d1l8ta_; d1e8xa4 boundaries correct). Correct PI3K accessory domain placements (a.118.1, b.7.1, d.15.1). Clear superfamily-level homology and shared Mg-ATP phosphotransfer mechanism; explicitly states substrate is family-level and even within d.144.1.6 varies, regulation not transferable, APH constitutive, PI3K regulated via other domains. Evidence requirements complete including Pfam-level family placement, catalytic residue checks, substrate assays, regulation data, orthology. No material errors.
